summary:
How in the world did you manage to obtain so many novels of mine? How in the world did you manage to read them all? Why in the world—well, allow me the pleasure of extracting a certain wild joy at thinking of someone caring that much. Thank you. 

As to what you missed ... as near as I can calculate, you have missed these novels: THE COSMIC PUPPETS (Ace Double) THE MAN WHO JAPED (Ace Double) 

THE PENULTIMATE TRUTH (Belmont) 

Now, about the stories. I made my first sale, a story to F&SF called “Roog”, in 1951, which is a long time ago. In 1953, for example, I had 27 stories appear that year. I cite these matters to convey to you that I, even I, can’t tell what you missed, although for four days my dutiful wife has been studying documents and trying vainly to list all the stories you appear to have missed. But there are just too many; you list having obtained 8 out of about 200, and incredible as it may seem I have no accurate way to produce a bibliography. I do not have copies of most of my published stories myself. I know this sounds nutty, but it is true. My favorite short story of my own is one called “Human Is”, and I can’t locate a copy of it anywhere—I may literally die without ever seeing a copy of it again. I remember A.E. van Vogt saying once that when some big hard-cover pub­ lisher approached him with the idea of putting out THE WORLD OF NULL A (it had only been a pulp serial up to then, and had long since left the stands for­ ever) van had only one copy to turn o...
